title: Sizing up Puente and Tito Rodriguez
summary: Both were good friends and talented; he did not mind because they played his music, and he saw himself as the champion playing challenger.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Okay. How would you size up Tito Puente, then?
A good friend. How would you size up Tito Rodriguez?
He was a good friend of mine too.
So in other words, the things that they did
sometimes when they wanted top billing over you and that, you didn't mind then?

No, I didn't mind. Secondly - - first of all, because you just can't stop a person to try to do his best or to get the best, because that's human nature. Secondly, because I know what they were doing. Any little thing that they were doing I know where they come from because they was playing my music, and third because I was older and I know how to control my emotions and I understand life better than --- they was --- They looked like they was fighting for the system.
Okay, then what they did never annoyed you.
I don't understand what you say.
What they did, in other words when they wanted top billing over you or they didn't want you to play with them. It didn't annoy you?

No, because if a person is running away from another one it must be a reason why. To me -- I always had the opportunity like a challenger, like a -- I was the champion, but I was playing the role of challenger. I want to be in the ring with them and they knew. They knew, they knew, they was avoiding to be in a sense, because they don't want to give a chance to anybody to have the slightest idea that I was the real thing or I was better. I never thought that I was better, I just always thinking that I was different.
